source.title: Understanding deep learning requires rethinking generalization
source.authors: Chiyuan Zhang; Samy Bengio; Moritz Hardt; B. Recht; O. Vinyals

record.tranche_reason: The study directly trains standard networks with random labels, corrupted labels and unstructured inputs, and measures training and test performance using the original intervention.
record.gate_note: The paper is an original source for V1–V5, so no verdict labels are assigned for those versions. Figure-only convergence and test-error curves are recorded without reconstructing values. Cited findings from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: This is the original randomization study: it trains networks with random labels, corrupted labels and randomized inputs, and measures fitting, convergence and generalization. It directly tests V1–V5. Its separate true-label and random-label learning curves do not establish the within-training ordering asserted by V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that successful architectures have sufficient effective capacity to memorize training data, conventional complexity measures struggle to explain their generalization, and empirical optimization ease persists without generalization. They also conclude that explicit regularization can improve generalization but does not fundamentally explain it.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses the original randomization intervention: train standard architectures with randomized labels or inputs under unchanged settings, then measure training and test performance.
record.method_sensitivity: The ImageNet Inception V3 result varies with explicit regularizers; CIFAR10 Alexnet fails to converge on random labels with weight decay. Convergence time and test error vary with label-corruption level.

fits_no_version.finding: The constructive ReLU expressivity theorem establishes representability of arbitrary finite-sample labels, without demonstrating SGD learning under unchanged settings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A two-layer ReLU network with 2n+d weights can represent any real-valued labeling of n distinct points in d dimensions.

record.problems: Several key curves are figure-only in the supplied text, without exact values. ImageNet Inception V3 does not reach perfect top-1 training accuracy on random labels under the reported settings. The explicit-regularization random-label results include an Alexnet failure and one MLP result below 100%.
record.rows_left_out: Rows for individual regularization combinations in Table 1 and Table 2 that do not bear directly on V5's claim were omitted; only representative true-label results with regularizers removed and the ImageNet no-regularizer result are retained. Figure 1 learning-curve details beyond the version-linked outcomes are omitted.

untested.parts: No ImageNet randomized-input experiment is reported; model-specific randomized-input outcomes for Alexnet and MLPs are not established by the cited figure.
The study does not test every architecture–regularizer combination; dropout is tested only with ImageNet Inception V3.

No measurement separates learning shared real-data patterns from memorizing noisy examples over time within a mixed-label training run. Separate learning curves for true and random labels do not establish that ordering.

missing.what: Central unregularized CIFAR10 random-label outcomes beyond Inception: Inception without BatchNorm has 100% train and 10.12% test accuracy; Alexnet 99.82% and 9.86%; MLP 3x512 100% and 10.48%; MLP 1x512 99.34% and 10.61%. These directly document near-perfect fitting with chance test performance and provide comparisons for the weight-decay experiments.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict labels are assigned because this study is an original source for V1–V5; V6 is untested. ImageNet's incomplete fitting and the Alexnet weight-decay failure are tested limitations, not untested parts. The modified augmentation schedule qualifies the record's blanket claim of unchanged settings. All judgments use only the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: The ImageNet Inception V3 experiment did not reach perfect training accuracy; its authors note that hyperparameter changes might achieve it.
The text describes a small constant-factor increase and quick convergence after fitting starts, but supplies no exact time values in the provided text.
Unstructured-input results are reported for CIFAR10 experiments; the text does not report them for ImageNet.
The text reports CIFAR10 sweeps and states that test error steadily worsens toward 90%; precise intermediate values are figure-only.

The study tests weight decay and augmentation on CIFAR10 and weight decay/dropout/augmentation on ImageNet; its random-label regularization experiments do not cover every model and regularizer combination.
